answer: Sybil resistance comes from slashable stake: every agent must lock collateral to earn one voting credential, and an arbiter can challenge any identity that reuses the same cedar seed. A cheater who floods the network with fake agents pays a bond for each one, so attack cost grows linearly with Sybil count. Since voting power follows locked stake, splitting a balance across wallets yields no extra influence. Honest validators receive nectar for catching fraud, while a bridge operator caught relaying the same identity twice forfeits its entire bond, making the attack unprofitable.
